summary: VDB S1 Green implementation correctly implements the seven-function observed-routing contract surface per test-strategy.md#phase-1 and test-strategy.md architecture guardrails: extractObservedRouting / classifyObservedRouting / runtimeModelStrict / computeRoleDefinitionHash / resolveStrict / classifyAgentFile / buildReceipt. All 10 observed-routing tests pass (10/10) at audited HEAD c224cc1 and at the post-housekeeping HEAD 29c00f8. extensions/measure-harness/index.ts extends the TaskReceipt interface with the 5 new fields (requestedModel/observedModel/observedAt/roleDefinitionHash/routingClassification) and wires the helpers into the task handler; the parent-fallback in runtimeModel is removed (the prior signature runtimeModel(agent, fallback) is now runtimeModel(agent), a strict wrapper around runtimeModelStrict(agent).model); the three routing-failure classifications (observed_routing_mismatch / observed_routing_unobservable / undeclared_child_pin) correctly cause the task to fail. Test imports match lib exports; every test has a one-line comment naming the contract section it protects; A3 probe asserts labeled {class,reason} structure; A7 probe asserts strict equality (no widening); A8 probe asserts symlink rejection; determinism probe asserts byte-identical stable fields. Gates: node --test tests/observed-routing.test.mjs exits 0 (10/10); 8 other shipped test files all green (78/78 in test:shipped); npm run test:shipped exits 0 (partition 9/2/0, with observed-routing AND sprint-state-machine in track-red); npm test exits 1 (14 sprint-state-machine failures, intentional-Red for parallel track); npm run check exits 0; node scripts/parity.mjs exits 1 fail-closed with ok=false, unmapped=2 (coder-openai-gpt-5-6-luna-fast and measure-adversarial-testing), modelMapMatches=true. ONE BLOCKING FINDING (F1): agents/change-quality-reviewer.md has no 'model:' frontmatter (confirmed via grep -c '^model:' = 0 and runtimeModelStrict({name:'change-quality-reviewer',model:undefined}) returns undeclared_child_pin), but lib/core.mjs#isTaskAllowed explicitly permits measure-orchestrator to dispatch to it (return childName.startsWith('measure-') || childName.startsWith('coder-') || childName === 'change-quality-reviewer'). With the strict runtime, every measure-orchestrator → change-quality-reviewer dispatch will now fail pre-spawn with undeclared_child_pin. The VDB S1 Green evidence handoff explicitly required 'verify every agent in agents/*.md has a model: frontmatter before Green closes, since the fallback's removal makes this a hard requirement'; this pre-flight condition was NOT met, and the regression was not caught. The agent file change-quality-reviewer.md has existed since e7f4277 (initial commit) and was hardened in 296cc2f, but never received a model: frontmatter. S1 acceptance cannot proceed until either (a) a model: frontmatter is added to agents/change-quality-reviewer.md, or (b) change-quality-reviewer is removed from the allowed-dispatch list in lib/core.mjs#isTaskAllowed. NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS: F2 the receipt's old 'model' field is retained as a silent alias to requestedModel (the strategy explicitly forbids this: 'A model field left on the receipt as a silent alias to requestedModel is forbidden (A7 analog)'). F3 lib/observed-routing.mjs#buildReceipt does NOT include observedAt in its return shape, even though the audit prompt and the handler's TaskReceipt interface both expect it; the handler compensates by computing observedAt from event.timestamp manually, so the field reaches the receipt but buildReceipt is incomplete relative to its documented contract. F4 the handler in extensions/measure-harness/index.ts manually composes the receipt using individual helpers (extractObservedRouting + classifyObservedRouting + computeRoleDefinitionHash) rather than calling the canonical buildReceipt primitive; functionally equivalent (all 5 fields populated correctly) but the architecture guardrail suggests buildReceipt should be the single composition point. F5 partition template: tests/observed-routing.test.mjs remains in tests/.track-red-files.txt at Green time (partition 9 shipped / 2 track-red / 0 unclassified). The test-strategy.md §Phase 1 says the file should be in the shipped surface and retired from track-red at S1 acceptance, not at Green; this is a documented deferral to acceptance. UX/API ergonomics: signature_consistency=pass (matches lib/core.mjs conventions: structured return values, pure functions, destructured inputs); error_structured=pass (every error carries a labeled class: verified_routing | unverified_routing | symlinked_agent_file | undeclared_child_pin + reason string when applicable); env_overridable=pass (pure module, no env coupling needed); deterministic=pass (no Date.now() / Math.random() / process.hrtime() in lib/observed-routing.mjs; buildReceipt returns byte-identical output for identical inputs); contract_match=pass (every documented symbol is exported and matches the test-strategy.md contract surface and the test assertions; minor field-naming discrepancies with the audit prompt's signature descriptions are noted under F3/F4 but do not contradict the implementation-vs-test-strategy contract).

findings.description: agents/change-quality-reviewer.md has no 'model:' frontmatter (zero matches for '^model:' in the file). parseAgentFile returns {name:'change-quality-reviewer', model:undefined, sourceModel:undefined}. With the VDB S1 Green runtimeModelStrict strict semantics, runtimeModelStrict({name:'change-quality-reviewer', model:undefined}) returns {error:{class:'undeclared_child_pin', role:'change-quality-reviewer'}}, and the task handler refuses dispatch pre-spawn with isError:true. However, lib/core.mjs#isTaskAllowed explicitly permits measure-orchestrator to dispatch to change-quality-reviewer: `return childName.startsWith('measure-') || childName.startsWith('coder-') || childName === 'change-quality-reviewer'`. The measure-orchestrator prompt (agents/measure-orchestrator.md line 115) instructs the orchestrator: 'Use change-quality-reviewer when an independent review adds value.' The permission table (line 47) explicitly allows delegation. The agent file change-quality-reviewer.md has existed since e7f4277 (initial commit) and was hardened in 296cc2f but never received a model: frontmatter. This regression was NOT pre-flighted by Jr Green: the green evidence handoff explicitly required 'verify every agent in agents/*.md has a model: frontmatter before Green closes, since the fallback's removal makes this a hard requirement'. Every other agent in agents/*.md (29 of 29) has a model: frontmatter — only change-quality-reviewer.md is missing. S1 acceptance cannot proceed until the regression is resolved.
findings.location: agents/change-quality-reviewer.md (line 1+ — frontmatter lacks 'model:' field); lib/core.mjs:357-359 (isTaskAllowed allows the dispatch); agents/measure-orchestrator.md:47,115 (orchestrator prompt relies on this dispatch)
findings.recommendation: Route to Green for fix before S1 acceptance: (option A) add a model: frontmatter to agents/change-quality-reviewer.md (the file is loaded by loadAgents, so adding e.g. model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna would make the role dispatchable; verify with `parseAgentFile('agents/change-quality-reviewer.md').model === MODEL_MAP[frontmatter.model]`); (option B) remove `|| childName === 'change-quality-reviewer'` from lib/core.mjs#isTaskAllowed and update agents/measure-orchestrator.md lines 47 and 115 to remove the change-quality-reviewer reference. Option A preserves existing orchestrator behavior with minimal blast radius.

findings.description: extensions/measure-harness/index.ts:335-336 writes BOTH 'model: modelRef' AND 'requestedModel: modelRef' to the receipt. The strategy explicitly forbids this: 'A model field left on the receipt as a silent alias to requestedModel is forbidden (A7 analog: aliasing the new field to the old one would mask the contract change).' The receipt's old `model` field should have been renamed to `requestedModel` (a breaking contract change), not duplicated. The green evidence acknowledged this: 'existing model field is retained as a compatibility alias to requestedModel — review-a should audit this for silent breakage on any consumer that reads receipt.model'. Today the `model` field is the only field written to the receipt's details consumer side, but the new `requestedModel` field is the new authoritative name.
findings.recommendation: Remove `model: modelRef` from the receipt shape at the next refactor; rely solely on `requestedModel: modelRef` (per the strategy). If a downstream consumer needs the old field, leave a TODO marker with a removal date. Alternative: keep `model` as the canonical field and rename `requestedModel` to a new field — but the strategy already established `requestedModel` as the new name.

findings.description: lib/observed-routing.mjs#buildReceipt returns {requestedModel, observedModel, roleDefinitionHash, promptHash, failureClassification, verifiedRouting} — 6 fields, no observedAt. The audit prompt's task description says 'buildReceipt({...}) — returns TaskReceipt with new fields requestedModel, observedModel, observedAt, roleDefinitionHash, routingClassification'. The handler in extensions/measure-harness/index.ts adds observedAt separately from event.timestamp and writes it to the receipt. Functionally the field reaches the receipt, but buildReceipt is incomplete relative to the audit prompt's stated contract (and is never called by the handler — see F4). The test-strategy.md contract header block in tests/observed-routing.test.mjs (which is the authoritative contract) does NOT include observedAt in buildReceipt's shape; it is consistent with the implementation. The discrepancy is between the audit prompt and the implementation, not between the implementation and the test contract.
findings.recommendation: Option A: update the audit prompt's signature description to match the test-strategy contract (recommended — the implementation matches the strategy). Option B: extend buildReceipt to take an observedAt input and emit it in the receipt shape, and have the handler pass event.timestamp through. Option A is preferred because the test-strategy is authoritative and the implementation matches it.

findings.description: extensions/measure-harness/index.ts#task manually composes the receipt (extractObservedRouting → classifyObservedRouting → computeRoleDefinitionHash) instead of calling the documented buildReceipt primitive. The 5 new receipt fields are correct (all populated, all values match), but the architecture guardrail in the strategy says 'the named-classification shape is part of the exported contract surface. Consumers (role_model_pool_20260805 Task 2.1, role_fitness_frontier_watch_20260805 Task 4.1) import from the same module' — i.e. consumers should import buildReceipt directly, not duplicate its composition logic. Two composition paths (lib's buildReceipt and the handler's manual composition) creates drift risk: a future contract change to buildReceipt could leave the handler out of sync.
findings.recommendation: Refactor the handler to call buildReceipt({pin: modelRef, roleDefinition: child.systemPrompt, promptBody: fullPrompt, events}) and merge the returned shape into the receipt, plus handle the observedAt field from event.timestamp separately (since buildReceipt does not return it — see F3). This aligns the handler with the documented contract primitive and reduces drift risk for downstream consumers.

findings.description: The audit prompt's task description diverges from the actual implementation in several places. (a) extractObservedRouting is described as returning `{observedModel, observedProvider, observedAt, source}` but actually returns `string | undefined` (the served model identifier). (b) runtimeModelStrict error is described as `{class: 'undeclared_child_pin', reason}` but actually returns `{class: 'undeclared_child_pin', role}`. (c) classifyRoutingFailure({requested, observed, runtime}) is described as a single helper but is NOT implemented — the equivalent behavior is achieved by compose of classifyObservedRouting + runtimeModelStrict. (d) resolveStrict(agentFilePath) is described but actually takes two strings `(requestedModel, observedModel)`. (e) computeRoleDefinitionHash(agent) is described but actually takes a systemPrompt string. (f) buildReceipt is described as returning `observedAt` but does not. The implementation matches the test-strategy.md contract header in tests/observed-routing.test.mjs and the test assertions. The discrepancies are in the audit prompt itself, not in the implementation. S1 Green evidence is internally consistent with the implementation; the audit prompt was likely written from a description of the contract that diverged from the final implementation.
findings.recommendation: Update the audit prompt's signature descriptions to match the implementation (or note the discrepancies as documentation drift in the strategy's contract header). The implementation is correct per test-strategy.md and the test assertions.
